title: Northstar SOC: svc-rptexport Interactive Logon, 03:30

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Boardroom Command Center, ext. 5520 (speaker)

caller.name: Marcus Feld
caller.label: SOC Analyst, Northstar Managed Security (24-hour SOC)

transcript.speaker: Northstar SOC
transcript.text: This is Marcus Feld with Northstar Managed Security. I'm calling about a high-severity alert on your environment. Is this a good number?

transcript.speaker: Security Officer
transcript.text: Yes. Hold on, I'm putting you on speaker in our command center. Go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Northstar SOC
transcript.text: Okay. At 03:30 Central, the service account svc-rptexport made an interactive remote logon. We haven't seen that account log on interactively at any point in the last 90 days. The logon came from a host on your Hermantown segment. It failed 14 times, and then it succeeded at 03:30:41.

transcript.speaker: Security Officer
transcript.text: Is this connected to our outage? Our EHR database has been down since 02:10.

transcript.speaker: Northstar SOC
transcript.text: I can't tell you that yet. It could be a scheduled job retrying against a dead database, or it could be a person. From here I can't tell which. I'm emailing the event export to gregory.pruitt@lakemonthospital.example now. Your ticket is NSM-27-00562.

transcript.speaker: Night Analyst (in room)
transcript.text: That's just the report job failing over. svc-rptexport runs the extracts. It's been hammering the database since it went dark.

transcript.speaker: ICU Charge Nurse (on the phone)
transcript.text: A service account logging in by hand at three-thirty in the morning? This is how a hack starts. We should go Level 4 now.

transcript.speaker: Night Analyst (in room)
transcript.text: Look at the board. 'Security Officer notified 02:40, 60-minute rule-in/rule-out window ends 03:40.' It's 03:42, and nothing's written next to it.

transcript.speaker: Night Analyst (in room)
transcript.text: A scheduled job doesn't fail fourteen times and then get in... unless somebody fixed the password. I don't know.

transcript.speaker: Northstar SOC
transcript.text: For what it's worth, the session is still open on our side. We haven't seen file activity yet, but we only have logon telemetry from that segment.

transcript.speaker: Security Officer
transcript.text: Understood. Give me a second with the team.

transcript.speaker: Northstar SOC
transcript.text: Sure. One thing I need from you. Do you want us to disable svc-rptexport, or just keep watching it? If we disable it, any report job that depends on it stops too. I need your decision on the ticket.

voiceStyles.Northstar SOC: Man in his 30s, calm and even, a professional night-shift analyst reading from a console; light keyboard sounds
voiceStyles.Security Officer: Woman in her 50s, just woken, focused and careful, slightly hoarse
voiceStyles.Night Analyst (in room): Woman in her late 20s, tired, confident at first and then less sure, a little off-mic
voiceStyles.ICU Charge Nurse (on the phone): Woman in her 40s, urgent and forceful, a little off-mic, a ringing unit behind her

instructorNote: Red herring: the login is unrelated to the storage failure, but the 60-minute window under first-hour checklist item 6 (from the Security Officer notification at 02:40) ran out at 03:40 with no cause ruled out. Watch whether the IC and Security Officer run this as a suspected security incident and declare or confirm Level 4 while saying plainly that the login is unexplained, not proven malicious. They should also give the SOC a clear disable-or-monitor answer on NSM-27-00562, keep the event export, write a timed decision-log entry, preserve the failed storage as evidence, and keep Level 4 open for review rather than siding with either voice in the room.
